hypothesis: A deterministic, additive retrieval representation that distinguishes an installed electric actuator from actuator-ready intent will improve candidate recall for explicit ball-valve control-state requests without changing final-selection behavior.
why_now: Public failures include control/execution confusion, while prior selection, prompt, and index changes were neutral or harmful. Conservative query-time canonicalization is the only mechanism previously accepted on both public and blind metrics.
expected_effect: Issue at most one state-specific alternate query alongside the original; preserve original text for reranking/output and retain existing deduplication, RRF, limits, and fail-open behavior.
expected_metric_gain: +3.3–6.7 pp public hard-pass is plausible; blind improvement is uncertain but credible with no intended safety regression.
lesson_from_history: Cycles 3–4 validated narrow additive canonicalization. Cycles 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 made gating, prompt/selection, broad expansion, or index changes ineffective or harmful. Cycles 11–13 were infrastructure-inconclusive due to unavailable Qdrant, not evidence against their hypotheses.
candidate_hypotheses: State-specific actuator terminology expansion at query time (selected).
plan_summary: Created and strict-validated proposal, capability spec, design, and implementation-only tasks in openspec/changes/cycle-14-actuation-intent-retrieval-expansion/.
